subject: Benchmark playbook: harness onboarding and test plan
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Laurent <sophie.laurent@fastretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark playbook: harness onboarding and test plan

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the performance qualification moving toward a reproducible benchmark run.

What we heard (summary)
- Latency SLO: target p50 <= 90ms for single-turn, ~512-token requests; p95 target to be agreed but we suggested <= 250ms as a starting point.
- Throughput requirement: steady-state 350 requests/sec (QPS) with occasional bursts to 500 QPS for short windows.
- Concurrency/backlog: expected 40-60 concurrent sessions; streaming partial responses required for chat flows.
- Workload shape: ~70% short queries (<64 tokens), 25% mid-length (64–512), 5% long (>512).

What we want to exchange this week
1) Your canonical prompt set (anonymized) + representative traces (we need tokenized requests and timestamps).
2) Any constraints on tokenization, special pre/post-processing, or business rules that affect output length.
3) Confirmation of acceptable adjacency for measuring streaming (do you want first-byte latency for streaming, or application-level perceived latency?).

What Redwood will deliver
- A measurement-spec PDF (attached) that defines: exact metrics (p50/p95 for first-byte and end-to-end, throughput sampling windows, concurrency measurement method), warmup procedure, and reproducibility checklist.
- A short harness onboarding doc (attached) and a runbook template so your SREs can execute a native reproducibility run in your environment or our dedicated capacity.
- We’ll propose two runs: an initial reproducibility run (canonical prompt set, single model variant, quantization-off) and a production-like run (with batching and recommended quantization).

Attachments I’m including: redwood_harness_instructions.md (quickstart for the harness) and measurement-spec-v1.pdf (draft).

Next steps
- Sophie: send anonymized prompt set + representative traces by EOD Thursday (we can accept CSV or JSONL).
- Karthik/Ben: we’ll prepare a short checklist for the warmup sequence (cache priming, 10-minute ramp, stable-window measurements).
- Book a 30-min reproducibility session — propose Friday 11:00am PT; I’ll set a calendar invite after Sophie confirms.

Thanks — happy to adjust if the targets above need to shift.

—
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment stubs:
- redwood_harness_instructions.md (text/markdown)
- measurement-spec-v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sophie Laurent <sophie.laurent@fastretail.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops-team@fastretail.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark playbook: harness onboarding and test plan

Thanks Monica — appreciate the clear recap. Attaching our prompt bundle and a small sample of traces. A few clarifications below.

Attachments included: fastretail_prompts_v2.csv, traces_sample.jsonl

Notes / clarifications
- Prompts: We removed all PII and replaced with placeholders. The file contains prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_length_bucket (short/mid/long), and a usage_weight column.
- Traces: sample includes timestamped requests and the application-side observed latency (for your reference). We can provide larger dumps if needed but would prefer secure transfer (S3 presigned) for full traces.
- Streaming: we care mostly about perceived speed for users in chat. Measuring first-byte for streaming is fine — we also value token-delivery cadence (i.e., per-200ms framing).
- Warmup: we typically prime model caches with ~200 unique prompts pre-flight. If your warmup guidance is different, we can align.

We’re available Friday at 11:00am PT — please send the invite.

—
Sophie Laurent
Head of ML Platform | FastRetail
sophie.laurent@fastretail.com

Attachment stubs:
- fastretail_prompts_v2.csv (text/csv)
- traces_sample.jsonl (application/jsonl)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sophie Laurent <sophie.laurent@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 12:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark playbook: harness onboarding and test plan

Great — thanks Sophie for the prompt bundle and traces. A couple of technical points I want to capture before the session so the reproducibility run is unambiguous.

Measurement specifics I recommend we lock today
- Metric definitions:
  • First-byte latency (streaming): time from request arrival to first token streamed.
  • TTF (time-to-full): time until the final token delivered.
  • Per-token cadence: median inter-token interval for streaming (report 50th/95th).
  • p50/p95 measured over steady-state windows of 60s; report a 10-minute aggregated run for stability.
- Warmup/warm-cache: run a deterministic priming sequence of 200 prompts (use the usage_weight ordering) followed by a 5-minute idle to allow KV-eviction equilibration. Record cache hit stats.
- Concurrency shaping: to simulate 40–60 concurrent sessions, we’ll use synthetic session generators that multiplex prompts at session-level pacing (rather than hammering with pure QPS). This better emulates your real session behavior.
- Batch settings: vendor-agnostic baseline run — batching disabled. Production-like run — adaptive batching up to 8 requests/batch with max-micro-batch latency budget 20ms.

Repro checklist items (for Friday)
1) Confirm tokenizer/version and whether you apply any custom truncation rules.
2) Confirm exactly which model checkpoint we should test (and whether quantized variants are allowed).
3) Provide a secure link (S3/GDrive) for full traces if we need end-to-end correlation.

I attached a compact harness checklist and the measurement-spec-v1.pdf Monica mentioned. I’ll present the suggested warmup and sampling windows in the Friday session.

—
Karthik Iyer
Staff Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Benchmark playbook: harness onboarding and test plan

Perfect — invite is sent for Friday 11:00am PT (calendar link included). Short agenda for that session:
- 10m: roles & objectives (who runs the harness, what success looks like)
- 10m: review measurement-spec highlights (metrics, windows, warmup)
- 10m: next steps + handoff (who provides artifacts, who runs the first reproducibility run)

Immediate asks (before the call)
- Sophie: share tokenizer/version and confirm the single checkpoint name to evaluate (or say "any of these" if you want multiple).
- Sophie/ops-team: provide S3 presigned link for the full traces if possible; otherwise we’ll work off the samples.
- Karthik/Ben: prepare a 1-page runbook we can hand to Sophie’s SREs (I attached a runbook-template.md stub).

I’ve attached a minimal runbook template and the two artifacts we referenced earlier. If there are any hard blockers (e.g., data-sharing approvals), flag them and we’ll escalate. Looking forward to the session.

Thanks,
Monica
